summary: Task 5 wiring of TelegramSender into BotService.sendTestMessage is clean against OWASP Top 10 (2021). The 422 stub is byte-identical to the pre-Wave-3 contract (code 'owner_chat_id_unknown' and message 'Send /start to your bot in Telegram first, then try again' preserved verbatim; HTTP status still flows through AppException.unprocessableEntity). The new IT helper seedConnectedBotWithRealEncryption encrypts a stable test constant via the real TokenEncryptor and persists only Base64(iv)/Base64(ciphertext) on the Bot doc — the plaintext VALID_TOKEN never returns from the helper, is never logged, and is never written to a response or audit event. testMessageMetadata exposes only Bot IDs (projectId, telegramBotId, chatId, messageId) — none token-shaped (A02 honoured). Failure-branch audit emission uses .doOnSuccess so BotService cannot double-write bot_test_message_sent on sender error; the unit test sendTestMessage_whenOwnerChatIdPresentAndSenderFails_propagatesError_noBotEvent pins this Decision-3 invariant. requireConnectedBot precondition unchanged (A01 ownership preserved). TEST_MESSAGE_BODY is a static constant with parseMode=null (A03 safe default per Decision 6). SecurityConfig untouched (A05). No new findings.
